description.p: ZenSight is a unified observability platform that bridges legacy monitoring protocols into Zenoh's pub/sub infrastructure. It provides a modern GUI for visualizing telemetry data from multiple sources.

ul.li: Real-time telemetry visualization from SNMP, Syslog, NetFlow, Modbus, and more
Network topology view with force-directed graph layout
Demo mode for testing without live bridges

description.p: The fleet release: three new sensors for what this infrastructure actually is. A Proxmox sensor that watches the hypervisor as a hypervisor — guest boot and firewall configuration, thin-pool over-commitment, backup outcomes and size trend; a container sensor that knows per-container memory, OOM kills, image digests and whether a healthcheck is failing or has never run at all; and an outside-in probe for HTTP, TLS, DNS and TCP, plus local certificate expiry. The SNMP sensor gains a per-device PDU budget and a one-shot discovery mode.
Nothing breaks: no wire contract moved and no existing default changed. See the CHANGELOG in the repository for the full list.

The operator release: ZenSight gains a model of itself as something that runs somewhere and must behave. A sensor can now see its own size and sheds load instead of dying, every state family's served schema is a gated contract, sensors are packaged one container per sensor with their own memory limits, and fleet configuration becomes desired state rather than hand-edited files — with a new read-only hostspec sensor holding each host to machine-checked assertions.
One deployment-breaking change: the SNMP sensor refuses to start on a v1/v2c configuration without an explicit opt-in flag. See the CHANGELOG in the repository for the full list and migration notes.

A month of accumulated work, and a release to read before upgrading: seventeen breaking entries, three of which break a deployment rather than an API. Every firing alert re-keys, the Prometheus scrape port moves to 127.0.0.1:9464, every exported SNMP series is renamed, and sensors and frontend must upgrade together. The features are the adaptive media plane — receiver-driven tier selection, a stream health panel, sink-sourced drop accounting — and a conformance harness that asks a running fleet in CI whether it obeys its own contract.
See the CHANGELOG in the repository for the full list, including breaking changes and migration notes.
Production profile hardening: the default-on TRW port-scan detector and the demo sentinel expectation are also disabled in production deployments.

Alert-noise release: the log novelty detector ("new log pattern" alerts) is removed, and sensor deployments default to a quiet production profile with the anomaly/security detector suite off. Telemetry, health and actionable ops alerts are unchanged.
See the CHANGELOG in the repository for the full list, including breaking changes and migration notes.
